Part 1: qPCR Reaction Preparation

    Step 1.1: Prepare a qPCR reaction master mix for the validation experiment. This master mix will contain all components except for the DNA templates. The volumes are calculated for 3 reactions plus one extra to account for pipetting inaccuracies.

        Option 1.1.1: Prepare the reaction master mix using the provided reagents.
            - Component A: Enhanced qPCR Master Mix
                - Recipe: 40 µL
            - Component B: Forward Primer (Allele-Specific)
                - Recipe: 7.4 µL of the 540 nM stock solution.
            - Component C: Reverse Primer
                - Recipe: 7.4 µL of the 540 nM stock solution.
            - Component D: nuclease-free water
                - Recipe: 17.2 µL

    Step 1.2: Mix the master mix thoroughly by gentle vortexing or pipetting, then centrifuge briefly to collect the contents at the bottom of the tube.

    Step 1.3: Aliquot the master mix into separate reaction wells or tubes suitable for the qPCR instrument.

        Option 1.3.1: Aliquot the master mix for the three experimental conditions.
            - Component A: Reaction Well 1 (Mutant)
                - Recipe: 18 µL of the prepared master mix.
            - Component B: Reaction Well 2 (Wild-Type)
                - Recipe: 18 µL of the prepared master mix.
            - Component C: Reaction Well 3 (NTC)
                - Recipe: 18 µL of the prepared master mix.

    Step 1.4: Add the specific DNA templates to the corresponding reaction wells.

        Option 1.4.1: Add the control and no-template samples to the aliquoted master mix.
            - Component A: Mutant-Type DNA Sample
                - Recipe: Add 2 µL to Reaction Well 1. The final volume will be 20 µL.
            - Component B: Wild-Type DNA Sample
                - Recipe: Add 2 µL to Reaction Well 2. The final volume will be 20 µL.
            - Component C: nuclease-free water
                - Recipe: Add 2 µL to Reaction Well 3 to serve as the No-Template Control (NTC). The final volume will be 20 µL.

    Step 1.5: Seal the reaction wells or tubes, mix by brief centrifugation, and load them into the real-time PCR instrument.

Part 2: Real-Time PCR Execution

    Step 2.1: Program the thermal cycler with the appropriate protocol for amplification and data acquisition.

        Option 2.1.1: Set up a 3-step thermal cycling program with a concluding melt curve analysis.
            - Component A: Initial Denaturation
                - Recipe: 95°C for 3 minutes. (1 cycle)
            - Component B: PCR Cycling
                - Recipe: Denaturation at 95°C for 10 seconds, followed by Annealing at 55°C for 30 seconds, and Extension at 72°C for 30 seconds. Data acquisition should be performed at the end of the extension step. (40 cycles)
            - Component C: Melt Curve Analysis
                - Recipe: 95°C for 15 seconds, followed by 60°C for 1 minute, then increase the temperature from 60°C to 95°C at a ramp rate of 0.5°C per step, with continuous data acquisition. (1 cycle)

    Step 2.2: Start the real-time PCR run.
